summary: Wenjie Qin specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Qin earned a PhD at Harvard University, studying under doctoral supervisor Tu Weiming as well as Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.
Werner Abraham was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna from 1962 to 1965. He held a post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich in 2002.
Wes Borton works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Borton studied at East Carolina University under Derek F. Maher and at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

Whalen Lai studied at International Christian University and Harvard University (~1968–1975). In Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, he held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (attested 1993) and the University of California, Davis (attested 2009).

Whitney Cox is an Indologist who studied at the University of Virginia (~1993–1997) and at the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~2000–2006). Cox also held a post at the University of Chicago (attested 2003).
Wilburn Hansen works in Japanology and religious studies. Hansen studied at the University of Colorado Boulder and at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith was a religious studies scholar who studied at Upper Canada College, the University of Toronto (~1934–1938), and Princeton University (~1944–1948). He held a post at Harvard University as 所長 (~1964–1973).

Wilfrid Sellars was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Michigan, Buffalo, and Oriel College. He held posts at Iowa (1938–1946), Minnesota (1947–1958), Yale (1958–1963), Pittsburgh (1963–1989), and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Linguist Wilhelm Deecke studied at Leipzig, Frederick William University Berlin, and Katharineum under Albrecht Weber, Franz Bopp, and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at Katharineum (1852–1855) and Ernestinenschule (1855–1870).

Wilhelm Geiger was an Indologist, Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, and linguist. He earned his PhD at Erlangen-Nuremberg under Friedrich von Spiegel, later holding posts at Neustadt, Munich, and Erlangen-Nuremberg.

Wilhelm Grube worked in sinology and linguistics, studying under Vasily Vasiliev and Georg von der Gabelentz, and at Leipzig University. He held an extraordinary professorship at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1892–1908).

Wilhelm Halbfass was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1967–1970), the University of Pennsylvania (~1973–2000), the University of Hamburg (1981–1982), and the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (~1990–1991).

Wilhelm Pertsch specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1853–1854) and under Albrecht Weber (1850) and Rudolf von Roth (~1854–1855).
Wilhelm Rau worked in Indology and linguistics. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (~1950–1952), Goethe University Frankfurt (1957), and the University of Marburg (~1957–1988).

Wilhelm Scherer was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Vienna (~1858–1860). He later held posts at the University of Vienna (~1868–1872) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1877–1886).

Wilhelm Schulze specialized in linguistics and Indology. He held posts at the University of Marburg (~1892–1895), the University of Göttingen (~1895–1902), and as professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1902–1932).

Wilhelm Streitberg was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig University (~1885–1888). He later held posts at the University of Münster (~1899–1909), Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1909–1920), and Leipzig University (~1920–1925).
Wilhelm Wackernagel worked in linguistics, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin from ~1824 to 1827. He held a post at the University of Basel from ~1833 to 1869.

Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy, studying at Frankfurt an der Oder, Göttingen, and Jena. He founded Humboldt University of Berlin in 1810 and held a post there the same year.
Will B. Miller works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Miller earned a PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Janet Gyatso, and also studied under Lopen Chorten in 2012.
